# Independent audit: the five-triangle owned-normal plane

Source: `candidate c42a2f528cc38b0c`.
Result: PASS. The source verifier passes 32 exact checks. The independent
checker `supporting computation verify_five_triangle_owned_normal_audit_slab_recovery.py` additionally
tests the displayed cap formulas by actual exact rational polygon clipping.

One harmless terminology repair was requested: the piecewise-affine real
radius function is concave, with strictly negative DISCRETE second
differences at all interior integer knots. It is not strictly concave
inside each affine segment. The proof only needs the former, correct
property, and the open-neighborhood compatibility argument is sound.

## 1. Full actual fibers and the velocity plane

The three discrete second differences of the baseline radius array are
-1/10. The mode e has second differences -3/5,16/5,-3/5, while the affine
mode j has zero second differences. Thus |a|+|b|<1/100 indeed keeps every
radius positive and all second differences negative. A positive concave
radius function over an interval defines a convex body r(z)T because
T is convex and contains zero. The projection is exactly [-2,2], giving
precisely the complete five integer fibers. No off-grid fiber modification
or sampling replacement is present.

All moment identities in (2) hold exactly, including the parity-restricted
weighted moments needed for first AREA variation. They are not incorrectly
replaced by unweighted radius sums. The area polynomial and its positive
Hessian are correct: R=817/200, E=114/25, M0=7353/400, and the quadratic
coefficients are 45 and 513/25.

## 2. Actual baseline depth and every competing fiber

At the middle centroid the own triangle contributes at least 2 and each
equal-radius reflected pair contributes twice its own centroid depth.
The complete ordinary triangle paired-depth theorem controls every
continuous direction and every integer tilt, including full/empty caps.
Their total is 2R=817/100. Vertical cuts are strictly more expensive.
The three canonical caps attain that value and cover all five continuous
fiber spaces. Hence the baseline raw GLOBAL maximum is exactly 817/100.

Equality first forces an own ordinary minimizing centroid direction.
For such a direction a reflected pair's sum is its zero-shift value
plus the positive square of the displacement until a full/empty
transition, after which it is at least one full triangle. Since one
full triangle is strictly larger than two 4/9 caps, only zero integer
tilt attains equality. Thus the three canonical directions exhaust the
middle minimizing menu, as needed for the later compact gap.

The nonmiddle upper bounds are valid for EVERY point, not just their
centroids. At an exposed endpoint, use a canonical vertex cap at the
point's largest barycentric coordinate; its own area is <=4/9 of the
fiber area, and a finite integer tilt isolates that fiber. At an inner
base use the same own-cap choice and a sufficiently large tilt toward
the adjacent outer endpoint, fully including it and excluding the
other side. Thus the exact bounds 32/25 and 937/200 apply fiberwise.
They are strictly below 817/100. These finite inequalities persist
under sufficiently small changes of the five radii.

## 3. Real critical slack groups and their drift sign

For |u|=1 and radii below 6/5, all triangle projections have absolute
value <3. Every off-source integer displacement has magnitude at least
one. Replacing a tilt beyond +/-3 by its same-sign endpoint +/-3
therefore preserves every off-source cap's zero/full mass, and preserves
the source cap. This supplies a common compact normal set for middle
and inner sources, including nearby bodies. Null line boundaries give
continuity and actual attainment. Vertical closed caps cannot lower
the infimum: large finite nonvertical tilts only remove some mass from
the tied source fiber and preserve all other statuses.

At the right inner centroid an attaining coefficient alpha<=0 would
put the four centroids at bases -2,-1,0,1 inside its cap. Their ordinary
Grunbaum contributions sum to exactly 689/100, larger than the finite
upper bound 937/200. This contradiction controls every continuous
direction, including alpha=0. Thus every attaining cap there has
alpha>0. Cyclic vertex-permutation maps are determinant-one linear
maps fixing zero. Their three dual normal images have sum zero and
span the plane, while the SAME raw integer coefficient is unchanged.
Their cap masses and through-source property are preserved. Therefore
they give an actual genuine critical circuit covering bases {1,2}.

Reflection gives the left circuit covering {-2,-1}. These source
groups are below the middle budget by strict slack. Frozen original
caps retain coverage and slack nearby; if desired, newly minimizing
slack caps retain the drift sign by the same strict inequality. No
smooth selection of their minimizing normals is needed. Cyclic
symmetry and convex depth superlevel sets justify that each chosen
inner centroid maximizes depth in its own fiber.

## 4. Normal optimization and the all-normal gap

The actual proper-vertex cap formula summed over the five triangles
has the displayed two moments R(a,b) and J(a,b)=10a. Completing its
square gives the unique nearby minimizer (theta,alpha)=(0,-2a) and
value D0=817/100+(228/25)b^2. The normal Hessian at the baseline is
diag(10,817/200). Along the optimized branch its determinant is
10(R+E b^2)>0, so the local branches remain nondegenerate.

The compact normal set from Section 3 is common to all nearby bodies.
At the original array the complement of small neighborhoods of the
complete three-element minimizing menu has a positive gap. Joint
continuity on that compact set preserves this gap; the stable proper
chambers and the implicit-function theorem identify the unique local
minimum in each neighborhood. This proves the actual all-normal depth
D0 nearby and does not infer globality from the stationary formula.

The three optimized middle caps cover the whole middle fiber; their
actual source attains D0. All nonmiddle points remain below D0 by the
strict finite-cap bounds already proved. Therefore the asserted GLOBAL
maximum is exactly D0 for sufficiently small (a,b).

## 5. Finite assignments and the quadratic costs

With equal cover weights, cyclic continuous balance forces a common
theta. The right and left assignments respectively impose sum alpha_i
<=0 and >=0. The slack group's only nonidentity row is strict. For
the right assignment, the free optimal tilts are feasible on a>=0.
On a<0 the mean-square bound forces the optimal equal tilt to zero.
The angular coefficient is positive, so theta=0 is optimal. This gives
exactly D0+20(a_-)^2; reflection gives D0+20(a_+)^2 for the left.

Choosing the assignment by the sign of a attains D0. Since every
through-middle-source cap has mass >=D0 by the independently proved
all-normal statement, this chosen value is also optimal without the
equal-weight/chamber restriction. The SEPARATE one-sided fixed-assignment
formulas are properly scoped to the specified equal-weight chamber;
only their quadratic jets extend to smoothly variable weights without
further proof. The initial integer drifts vanish, so weight derivatives
do not change the first drift row.

The frozen cap Hessian is 40A^2+(456/25)B^2. Free normal optimization
removes exactly 40A^2. A wrong-sided assignment restores 40A^2 per
cap, and the correct assignment restores zero. Multiplying the three
cap sum by 3/4 and subtracting from the mass Hessian gives precisely
90(A_+)^2 for the right assignment and 90(A_-)^2 for the left. The
B term cancels exactly rather than being omitted.

## 6. Actual fixed-budget scaling and scope

The common continuous homothety with k^2=R/(R+E b^2), accompanied by
the same k scaling of each cap's integer coefficient, maps each
original cap exactly to its image and scales all areas by k^2.
It preserves lattice bases, sources, ownership signs, compatibility,
and strict slack. The actual GLOBAL depth becomes Q, while total
area becomes M0+45R a^2/(R+E b^2). This is a strict fixed-budget
volume gain exactly when a!=0. The whole b-axis is exactly neutral.

The baseline normalized maximum is 4/9, above the target 2/9. The
note correctly asserts neither a below-target descent theorem nor
the existence of similarly useful slack groups for arbitrary bodies.
